```{r load-lib, message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r load-data}
# load your data 
sample_submission <- read_csv("data/sample_submission.csv")
test <- read_csv("data/test.csv")
train <- read_csv("data/train.csv")
```

```{r cleaning}
# Cleaning sample_submission
glimpse(sample_submission)
sum(is.na(sample_submission))
#sample_submission is clean by default
```

```{r cleaning}
# Cleaning train

train <- train %>%
  select(Id,OverallQual,GrLivArea,YearBuilt,Neighborhood,MSZoning,LotFrontage,SalePrice)

train %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~n_distinct(.x))) %>%
  select(where(~.x == 0))

# demonstrates that there are no columns with no arguments, hence this data frame must have no useless columns.
```

```{r cleaning}
# Cleaning test

test <- test %>%
 select(Id,OverallQual,GrLivArea,YearBuilt,Neighborhood,MSZoning,LotFrontage)
test <- test %>%
  mutate(OverallQual = case_when(
    OverallQual > 7 ~ "High Qual",
    OverallQual < 4 ~ "Low Qual",
    OverallQual > 3 & OverallQual < 8  ~ "Med Qual"))

test %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~n_distinct(.x))) %>%
  select(where(~.x == 0))

# Shows that there are no columns with no arguments, hence this data frame must have no unnecessary columns
```

# We have worked out that the mean price and median price is the same to 3 significance figure accuracy, this suggests that the distribution of sales price for housing could be approximated to a normal distribution.

```{r}

train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    # log-transform target
    log_saleprice = log(SalePrice),
  )

# Original SalePrice
ggplot(train, aes(x = SalePrice)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of SalePrice")

# Log-transformed SalePrice
ggplot(train, aes(x = log_saleprice)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of log(SalePrice)")


```

#The raw SalePrice distribution was highly right-skewed. We applied a natural log transformation, which produced a more symmetric distribution and better supported linear model assumptions.

```{r}

train <- train %>%
  mutate(OverallQual = case_when(
    OverallQual > 7 ~ "High Qual",
    OverallQual < 4 ~ "Low Qual",
    OverallQual > 3 & OverallQual < 8  ~ "Med Qual"))
```

```{r}
train <- train %>%
  mutate(
  OverallQual = fct_relevel(as.factor(OverallQual), "Low Qual", "Med Qual", "High Qual"))
```

# In our Log Sale Price Against Median Quality plot, there seems to be an overall trend from quality equals 2 to 10, with an anomoly at 1. By counting how many data points were given for each score, it is clear that the anomoly is a cause due to lack of data, hence unreliable. It is difficult to assume a general correlation for scores with few data points, where scores with much data points has suggested that the SalePrice does not increase, at least not significantly due to the quality assessed.

```{r}

#OVERALLQUAL

ggplot(train, aes(x = factor(OverallQual), y = log_saleprice)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#6AAEDF") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "log(SalePrice) by Overall Quality",
    x = "Overall Quality",
    y = "log(SalePrice)"
  )
```

# From our scatter point plot when adjusted to standard error, we can see that there is a correlation visually between SalePrices and LotArea, predicting a possible dependency. The standard error increases as we approach greater values in LotArea and SalePrices, which suggests possible outliers, but also due to the lack of data.

```{r}

# GRLIVAREA

ggplot(train, aes(x = GrLivArea, y = log_saleprice)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "log(SalePrice) vs Above-Ground Living Area",
    x = "GrLivArea (sq ft)",
    y = "log(SalePrice)"
  )

```

```{r}

# YEARBUILT

ggplot(train, aes(x = YearBuilt, y = log_saleprice)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "darkgreen") +

  labs(
    title = "log(SalePrice) vs Year Built",

  )

```

```{r}

#NEIGHBORHOOD

ggplot(train, aes(
      x = reorder(Neighborhood, log_saleprice, FUN = median),
      y = log_saleprice)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.2) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "log(SalePrice) by Neighborhood",
    x = "Neighborhood (ordered by price)",
    y = "log(SalePrice)"
  )
```

```{r}

#MSZoning

```

```{r}

#LOTFRONTAGE
```

```{r}
# Model 1 — structural only
mod1 <- lm(log_saleprice ~ GrLivArea + OverallQual + YearBuilt, data = train)

# Model 2 — structural + location + amenities
mod2 <- lm(log_saleprice ~ LotFrontage + Neighborhood + MSZoning,
           data = train)

# Compare adjusted R2
summary(mod1)$adj.r.squared
summary(mod2)$adj.r.squared

```


```{r}
train_rec_1 <- recipe(
  log_saleprice ~ GrLivArea + OverallQual + YearBuilt,
  data = train) %>%
  step_unknown(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())
train_mod_1 <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm")
train_wflow_1 <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(train_mod_1) %>%
  add_recipe(train_rec_1)
```

```{r}
train_fit_1 <- train_wflow_1 %>%
  fit(data = train)
tidy(train_fit_1)

```

```{r}
train_test_1 <- predict(train_fit_1, test, type = "numeric") %>%
  bind_cols(test)
glimpse(train_test_1)

train <- train%>%
 mutate(log_avg_price = mean(log_saleprice))
```

```{r}
train <- train %>%
  mutate(Mag_Price = case_when(
    log_saleprice > log_avg_price ~ "High Qual",
    log_saleprice < log_avg_price ~ "Low Qual"),
    Mag_Price = fct_relevel(Mag_Price, "Low Qual", "High Qual"))
train
```

```{r}
test <- test %>%
  mutate(Mag_Price = case_when(
    log_saleprice > log_avg_price ~ "High Qual",
    log_saleprice < log_avg_price ~ "Low Qual"),
    Mag_Price = fct_relevel(Mag_Price, "Low Qual", "High Qual"))
```


```{r}
train_rec_2 <- recipe(
  Mag_Price ~ GrLivArea + OverallQual + YearBuilt,
  data = train) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())
train_mod_2 <- logistic_reg() %>%
  set_engine("glm")
train_wflow_2 <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(train_mod_2) %>%
  add_recipe(train_rec_2)
```

```{r}
train_fit_2 <- train_wflow_2 %>%
  fit(data = train)
tidy(train_fit_2)

```

```{r}
train_test_2 <- predict(train_fit_2, test, type = "prob")
glimpse(train_test_2)
```
